record.paper_title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
record.original_question: Classify all finite chiral polyhedra in Euclidean 4-space E^4.

evidence.quote: Problem 38 Classify all finite chiral polyhedra in E4.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A polyhedron in Euclidean 4-space $\mathbb{E}^4$ is a discrete geometric structure $P$ consisting of vertices (points in $\mathbb{E}^4$), edges (line segments joining pairs of vertices), and faces (finite or infinite planar or skew polygons), together with prescribed incidences, such that (i) each edge lies in exactly two faces, (ii) the vertex-figure at every vertex (the polygon whose vertices are the neighbors of that vertex and whose edges join consecutive neighbors as one traverses the faces around the vertex) is a single finite polygon, (iii) $P$ is connected (its edge graph is connected), and (iv) $P$ is discrete (every compact subset of $\mathbb{E}^4$ meets only finitely many faces). The geometric symmetry group $G(P)$ is the group of isometries of $\mathbb{E}^4$ that permute the vertices, edges, and faces of $P$. The polyhedron $P$ is called chiral if $G(P)$ has exactly two orbits on the flags (incident triples vertex–edge–face) of $P$ such that adjacent flags lie in different orbits, equivalently if $G(P)$ acts transitively on the rotational flag-classes but $P$ admits no symmetry reversing the orientation of its flags. Finally, $P$ is finite if it has only finitely many vertices, edges, and faces.

Classify, up to similarity of $\mathbb{E}^4$, all finite chiral polyhedra in $\mathbb{E}^4$.
artifact.status_search_result: A full classification of finite chiral polyhedra in $\mathbb{E}^4$ does not appear in the literature. Individual finite chiral 4-polytopes in $\mathbb{R}^4$ have been constructed (e.g., Cunningham–Pellicer, 2014), and constructions of finite abstract chiral 4-polytopes are known, but no complete geometric classification of finite chiral polyhedra (rank-3 structures) in 4-dimensional Euclidean space has been published. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A Finite Chiral 4-Polytope in R^4
status_evidence.snippet: A chiral 4-polytope in projective 3-space yields a finite chiral 4-polytope in Euclidean 4-space.
status_evidence.claim: Individual finite chiral examples in dimension 4 have been found, but no complete classification of finite chiral polyhedra in E^4 is given.

status_evidence.title: Chiral Polyhedra in 3-Dimensional Geometries and from a Petrie–Coxeter Construction
status_evidence.snippet: Classifications focus on chiral polyhedra in 3-dimensional ambient geometries; the 4-dimensional finite case remains a subject of construction rather than complete classification.
status_evidence.claim: Classification work is ongoing; the 4-dimensional finite case has not been completed.
